search.

milestone. The relevant normalizer/quotient foundations are already in the
pinned mathlib. The external projects below contain related constructions,
but their inspected declarations either specialize to a different mathematical
problem or simply wrap existing mathlib results. Adding them would create
version and dependency work without supplying a missing proof.

the rejected candidates were not compiled, their transitive axioms were not
audited, and their kernel declarations were not replayed. Source inspection,
README claims, CI badges, and `#check` would not suffice for acceptance.

# External Lean prerequisites for the full Lemma 2.8

Research date: 2026-11-14. This search concerns the full Artin–Coxeter
normalizer-quotient surjectivity problem, beyond the completed generalized
kernel milestone. Read `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` fully before research.
No current proof-package file was edited by this search.

## Decision and verification boundary

**TauCetiProject/TauCeti is a directly useful source candidate.** It contains
the actual Artin group given by the braid presentation, its canonical
projection to a Coxeter system, strong exchange, arbitrary standard
parabolic minimal representatives, and Matsumoto's theorem. These are proved
from definitions compatible with mathlib's Coxeter presentation, rather than
from a class assuming the desired normalizer lifting conclusion.

This report records source inspection only. It does **not** accept any
external theorem as independently verified. Compilation of the selected
closure, complete elaborated statements/definitions, transitive axiom audit
(excluding `sorryAx` and custom axioms), and fresh kernel replay are required
before reuse. Root coordinates those checks against the package's pinned
dependencies. No toolchain installation, `lake update`, cache operation,
dependency build, or shared package mutation was performed by this search.

No inspected source supplies the final normalizer-quotient surjectivity
theorem itself. Its remaining local proof must show that a minimal Coxeter
normalizer representative lifts to an Artin normalizer element, then pass to
the already formalized quotient map. Surjectivity of the ambient projection
alone does not prove surjectivity on normalizers or their quotients.

## TauCetiProject/TauCeti: preferred supplier

- Repository: <https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti>.
- Inspected SHA: `62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9`.
- Toolchain: `leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0-rc2`.
- Manifest mathlib SHA: `e8ba86fa9744dd8d90f48c1752bc735f61a4ca81`.
- License: Apache-2.0, confirmed in root `LICENSE` and source headers.
- Isolated source checkout: `/tmp/lemma28-full-search/tauceti`.

The current kernel package pins the same Lean version and mathlib
`65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9`, so compatibility must be checked;
this report does not infer it from the matching Lean version.

### Exact canonical presentation and projection

Read the full
[`Artin.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Artin.lean).
Its declarations are in namespace `TauCeti`:

- `artinRelation M i i'` is the free-group product of the two length
  `M i i'` braid words, with the second inverted.
- `artinRelationsSet M` is the range of all those relators.
- `ArtinGroup M` is **definitionally**
  `PresentedGroup (artinRelationsSet M)`, not a replacement group.
- `ArtinGroup.gen M i` is `PresentedGroup.of i`.
- `ArtinGroup.prod_map_gen_braidWord M i i'` proves the defining relation.
- `ArtinGroup.lift` is proved using `PresentedGroup.toGroup`.
- `ArtinGroup.toCoxeterGroup cs : ArtinGroup M →* W`, for an ordinary
  `cs : CoxeterSystem M W`, sends every Artin generator to `cs.simple i`.
- `ArtinGroup.toCoxeterGroup_surjective cs` proves ambient surjectivity from
  generation by simple reflections. It has no surjectivity premise.

The diagonal entry `M i i = 1` gives identical one-letter words and hence a
trivial relator; it does not impose the square relation. Infinite entries
are encoded by zero, for which both words are empty and the relator is also
trivial. Reversing which alternating word is listed first only inverts a
relator and does not change the braid equation. Choosing `W := M.Group` and
`cs := M.toCoxeterSystem` specializes this to mathlib's actual Coxeter
presentation. These checks rule out the relevant semantic shortcuts.

There is no Artin standard-parabolic definition in this module. Locally
defining `Subgroup.closure (ArtinGroup.gen M '' J)` gives the intended
subgroup generated by the Artin generators. Its image under the canonical
projection must be proved equal to `cs.parabolic J`, using the generator
formula and closure/map API. This is an outstanding integration obligation,
not an extra hypothesis to assume.

### Exact minimal-representative suppliers

Read the parabolic definitions, reduced-word membership lemmas, minimality
proofs and Deodhar lemma in
[`Parabolic.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Parabolic.lean).
These extend namespace `CoxeterSystem`, with ordinary
`{B W : Type*} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix B}` and `cs : CoxeterSystem M W`:

- `cs.parabolic J := Subgroup.closure (cs.simple '' J)` (line 115).
- `exists_isReduced_wordProd_eq_of_mem_parabolic` (line 192): an element
  of `cs.parabolic J` has a reduced expression with all letters in `J`.
- `IsMinimalCosetRep J u := ∀ v ∈ cs.parabolic J,
  cs.length u ≤ cs.length (u * v)` (line 256).
- `exists_isMinimalCosetRep J w` (line 263):
  `∃ v ∈ cs.parabolic J, cs.IsMinimalCosetRep J (w * v)`.
- `length_mul_of_isMinimalCosetRep hu hv` (line 307):
  `length (u * v) = length u + length v`, for minimal `u` and
  `v ∈ cs.parabolic J`.
- `existsUnique_isMinimalCosetRep_mul J w` (line 357): unique factorization
  `w = p.1 * p.2` with minimal `p.1` and parabolic `p.2`.
- `IsMinimalCosetRep.simple_mul_or_exists_eq_mul_simple` (line 488):
  `cs.IsMinimalCosetRep J (cs.simple i * u) ∨
  ∃ j ∈ J, cs.simple i * u = u * cs.simple j`.

All these statements allow arbitrary `J : Set B`; no finite-rank or
finite-Coxeter-group hypothesis occurs. `IsMinimalCosetRep` concerns the
coset `u W_J`; multiplication-side conventions must be retained in the
local normalizer proof.

### Exact Matsumoto supplier

Read the complete
[`Matsumoto.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Matsumoto.lean)
and the definitions/soundness proof in `BraidEquivalence.lean`.
`CoxeterSystem.BraidEquivalent M` is `Relation.EqvGen` of the inductive
single braid replacement inside a prefix/suffix. It is not defined as
equality of evaluations.

`TauCeti.braidEquivalent_of_isReduced_wordProd_eq cs hω hω' hprod`
proves braid equivalence of reduced words with equal Coxeter product.
`TauCeti.matsumoto cs f hbraid hω hω' hprod` states

```lean
(ω.map f).prod = (ω'.map f).prod
```

for any `[Monoid G]`, `f : B → G`, and the actual braid-relation equations
`hbraid`. It requires no involution relation on `f`. Applying it to
`ArtinGroup.gen M` and `ArtinGroup.prod_map_gen_braidWord M` gives
well-defined positive reduced-word lifts in the actual Artin group.

`TauCeti.existsUnique_reducedWordLift cs f hbraid` (line 192) concludes

```lean
∃! F : W → G, ∀ ω : List B, cs.IsReduced ω →
  F (cs.wordProd ω) = (ω.map f).prod
```

This is a function, not a multiplicative homomorphism. Local integration
must prove the length-additive multiplication rule and the projection
formula; their truth must not be silently encoded as typeclass fields.
No finiteness assumption appears in these Matsumoto statements.

The proof performs induction on word length. Different initial letters are
connected through the proved rank-two descent lemma in `Dihedral.lean`;
`Geometric.Basic.lean` proves the exact order of products of simple
reflections from the concrete real geometric representation. The statements
use mathlib's ordinary presentation-based `CoxeterSystem`, not a new class
whose fields assume exchange or Matsumoto.

### Closure and source-hole screen

Following actual local imports from Artin and Matsumoto gives ten TauCeti
modules: `GroupTheory.Coxeter.{Artin,Basic,BraidEquivalence,Dihedral,
Geometric.Basic,Matsumoto,Parabolic,StrongExchange}` and
`Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.{Angle,Bounds}`. The generated
list is `/tmp/lemma28-full-search/tauceti/lemma28-closure.txt`.
All remaining imports in that closure are mathlib.

Source searches found no `sorry`, declaration of `axiom`, `unsafe`, or
`opaque` in the Coxeter subtree or in the two trigonometric suppliers.
This is only a source screen: imported axioms, elaboration and compilation
must still be checked. No theorem is accepted merely because this screen
passes.

# Landmark 1: GitHub source search for actual geometric freeness

Date: 2026-11-14. Target: the standard contragredient action of an arbitrary
finite Coxeter group, an arbitrary subset `J` of its simple indices, the real
point stabilizer theorem, and freeness of the actual `N_W(W_J)/W_J` action
on the actual relative complexified complement. Crystallographic-only
results are insufficient.

## Decision

The best directly relevant new formal supplier is still TauCeti's generic
geometric-sign development. It provides the root signs and simple-reflection
permutation of positive roots needed for a local proof of the point-stabilizer
theorem. It does not already state that theorem or complexified-complement
freeness. No directly usable general point-stabilizer/chamber theorem was
found in the additional GitHub candidates inspected.

The exact upstream Sign import closure contains nine TauCeti modules,
155,476 bytes. Seven modules are already in the unchanged parent package.
Only `Geometric/RankTwo.lean` and `Geometric/Sign.lean` are new, totaling
21,094 upstream bytes. At the parent's subsequent authorization these were
prepared under the separate `landmarks/vendor/` tree. Lake's first build
attempt with their original module paths resolved dependencies through the
parent library and failed. The parent then authorized mechanical relocation:

- `ArtinLandmarkVendor.Geometric.RankTwo` has unchanged source bytes;
- `ArtinLandmarkVendor.Geometric.Sign` substitutes its one RankTwo import
  with `ArtinLandmarkVendor.Geometric.RankTwo`;
- the original exact upstream sources remain as `.lean.txt` under
  `landmarks/vendor/upstream/`;
- mathematical declaration namespaces, statements and proofs are unchanged.

`landmarks/vendor/provenance.json` records both upstream/local hashes,
paths, the exact single import patch, all old-module references and mathlib
roots. The relocated local Lean source total is 21,086 bytes. This search
does not assert that compilation, transitive axiom audit, or kernel replay
of those sources has passed. The parent owns those acceptance checks. No

## Direct generic supplier: exact APIs and hypotheses

In
[TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Geometric/Sign.lean](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Geometric/Sign.lean#L140),
the ambient parameters are just

```lean
{I W : Type*} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix I} (cs : CoxeterSystem M W)
```

There is no finiteness, crystallographic, positive-definiteness, or
root-pairing hypothesis. Write `ρ = cs.geometricRepresentation` and
`α i = Finsupp.single i (1 : ℝ)`. The exact useful conclusions are:

```lean
cs.geometricRepresentation_single_pos_iff (w : W) (i : I) :
  0 < ρ w (α i) ↔ ¬ cs.IsRightDescent w i

cs.geometricRepresentation_single_neg_iff (w : W) (i : I) :
  ρ w (α i) < 0 ↔ cs.IsRightDescent w i

cs.geometricRepresentation_injective : Function.Injective ρ

cs.geometricRoots : Set (I →₀ ℝ) :=
  {v | ∃ (w : W) (i : I), ρ w (α i) = v}

cs.pos_or_neg_of_mem_geometricRoots (hv : v ∈ cs.geometricRoots) :
  0 < v ∨ v < 0

cs.ne_zero_of_mem_geometricRoots (hv : v ∈ cs.geometricRoots) : v ≠ 0

cs.geometricReflection_pos_of_mem_geometricRoots
    (hv : v ∈ cs.geometricRoots) (hpos : 0 < v) (hne : v ≠ α i) :
  0 < M.geometricReflection i v

cs.bijOn_geometricReflection_geometricRoots (i : I) :
  Set.BijOn (M.geometricReflection i)
    {v | v ∈ cs.geometricRoots ∧ 0 < v ∧ v ≠ α i}
    {v | v ∈ cs.geometricRoots ∧ 0 < v ∧ v ≠ α i}
```

The strict order on `Finsupp` means coordinatewise nonnegative and nonzero
for `0 < v`; it does not mean every coordinate is strictly positive.
The file also proves invariance of `geometricRoots` under `ρ w` and
negation. Its rank-two input is a proof via explicit trigonometric
coefficients, not an assumed root-sign property.

correct new import is `ArtinLandmarkVendor.Geometric.Sign`.

TauCeti.stabilizer_eq_closure_wallReflections

    {x : M} (hx : x ∈ TauCeti.dominantChamber P b) :

## Missing bridges and a concrete generic proof route

The Sign supplier supports the following independent local route. These are
remaining obligations, not source results claimed to have been proved here:

1. Derive finite index type from `simple_injective` and finite `W`, then finite
   roots from their explicit `W × I` parametrization. Let `δ` be the sum
   of all positive geometric roots. The positive-root permutation theorem
   gives `ρ(s_i) δ = δ - 2 α_i`. Maximize `φ(ρ(w)δ)` over finite `W`;
   comparing with simple-reflection translates puts a conjugate of `φ`
   in the closed dominant chamber. This works on the actual dual standard
   representation without crystallographic assumptions.
2. Prove the dominant-point stabilizer theorem by length descent. If
   dominant `φ` is fixed by `w ≠ 1`, choose a left descent `i` of `w`.
   The Sign theorem makes `ρ(w⁻¹)α_i` negative. Its evaluation under `φ`
   equals `φ(α_i)` by invariance, while dominance makes the former
   nonpositive and the latter nonnegative. Hence `φ(α_i)=0`, so `s_i`
   fixes `φ`. Shorten `w` and induct to show that the stabilizer is
   generated by the simple reflections whose simple-root values vanish.
   Conjugate back for arbitrary real points.
3. Connect this to root-reflection generation for the actual root kernels
   and to `W_J`. A convenient route avoids proving a complete parabolic
   root-subsystem equality: define the dominant functional `c_J` with
   simple-coordinate values zero on `J` and one outside `J`. The dominant
   stabilizer theorem gives `Stab(c_J)=W_J`. A root `β` in the span of
   `J` has `c_J(β)=0`; its conjugated simple reflection fixes `c_J` by
   the geometric root-reflection formula, hence belongs to `W_J`.
   Establishing that reflection formula and the functional/span comparison
   are explicit remaining bridges. Ordinary parabolic length theory alone
   does not assert them.
4. For a pair `(φ,ψ)` in the actual relative complement, choose a real
   `t` avoiding the finitely many cancellations for root evaluations.
   Then roots vanishing on `φ+tψ` are exactly those vanishing on both
   `φ` and `ψ`; by complement membership every such root annihilates all
   of `Θ_J`, hence lies in the span of `J`. Any element fixing the pair fixes that real
   combination, so the stabilizer theorem places it in `W_J`. Combined
   with the proved trivial action of `W_J`, this gives the desired
   freeness of the quotient group, once all action/model bridges are made.
5. Invoke the actual finite-action quotient-covering construction only after
   freeness. Pinned mathlib has `Finite.to_properlyDiscontinuousSMul` and
   `isQuotientCoveringMap_quotientMk_of_properlyDiscontinuousSMul` under
   continuous constant action, Hausdorff locally compact total space and
   `IsCancelSMul`. An injective representation alone does not prove free
   action on points; a finite group alone only supplies proper discontinuity.

No external proof is accepted from this search alone. Source suitability,

and correspondence to the actual geometric statement remain distinct checks.
No mathematical literature error was established in these readings.

**Positive Artin prerequisites are present as concrete source candidates.**

actual braid presentation, constructs its canonical map to the actual
presented Artin group, and proves spherical embedding, cancellation,
fractions, left/right gcd existence and left lcm existence. It also proves
the precise positive-lift divisibility/weak-order correspondence used in
Lemma 5.9 and identifies divisors of the fundamental element with reduced
Coxeter lifts.

**No reduced ribbon groupoid, its complete relations, or Theorem 5.6
normalizer decomposition was found.** These positive results do not by
themselves prove the requested landmark. They are candidates for filling
prerequisites, not a replacement definition of the ribbon groupoid or an
assumption of the normalizer conclusion.

- Definition 5.1 has actual Artin elements as arrows, satisfying

- Equations (5.2)–(5.4) define positive elementary ribbons from parabolic
  fundamental elements; Definition 5.5 generates the reduced subgroupoid
  using these particular arrows.
- Theorem 5.6 asserts the actual normalizer decomposition

- Remark 5.7/(5.8) uses the positive left lcm and its two generating-ribbon
  expressions; the cited completeness of these relations is an additional
  theorem, not a consequence of ordinary Matsumoto.
- Lemma 5.9 uses the order isomorphism between positive reduced Coxeter
  lifts and weak left divisibility, as well as the actual ribbon/lcm

# Landmark 2: spherical Artin and reduced-ribbon supplier search

Date: 2026-11-14. Scope: formal suppliers for the actual reduced ribbon
groupoid of `TauCeti.ArtinGroup M`, under finiteness of the actual Coxeter
group `M.Group`, with arbitrary `J` and no crystallographic restriction.
Only this document was edited; candidate sources and search receipts were
staged under `/tmp/artin-landmark2-search/other/`. No mathematical code,
configuration, vendor source, dependency pin, or shared cache was changed.

## Decision

No additional external source passed the direct-use screen for the actual
spherical-Artin reduced-ribbon/normalizer identification or its complete
presentation. The search did find an actual positive `B₃` word-normal-form
development and actual cancellation proofs for a countably generated
ordinary braid monoid. Their literal statements do not quantify over a
Coxeter matrix, do not cover all spherical types, and do not identify reduced
ribbons with the normalizer quotient. Other Garside/ribbon name matches
concern formal rewrite syntax, punctured-torus braid monoids, or specific
rank-two presentations.

Consequently no rejected external candidate was installed, compiled,
axiom-audited or kernel-replayed. None is accepted as a formally verified
supplier by this search. A README, a source comment advertising theorem
counts, an audit command in source, or an absence of textual `sorry` would
not replace the required build, transitive axiom audit and kernel replay.

## Exact target and missing strength

Read the original article's §5, Definitions 5.1 and 5.5, Theorem 5.6,
Remark 5.7 and Lemma 5.9 from `/tmp/theorem18-source.txt` (arXiv:2509.21915v3,
PDF pp. 21–23). The larger ribbon groupoid has actual Artin elements as
morphisms:

```text
Hom_R'(I,K) = { β ∈ A | A_I^+ β = β A_K^+ }.
```

Here `A_I^+` is the submonoid generated by the selected actual Artin
generators. The reduced groupoid is generated by the positive ribbons
`μ_(a,I)=Δ_I⁻¹ Δ_(I∪{a})`, with the appropriate target subset. The
required structural theorem identifies the normalizer with the semidirect
product of the actual parabolic subgroup and the actual reduced-ribbon
vertex subgroup. Its quotient consequence is the desired vertex-group
identification. A complete presentation additionally needs relations among
the ribbon generators to be complete, rather than merely true after
evaluation in the Artin group.

Defining `A^+` directly as a submonoid of the actual Artin group is legitimate
and avoids needing a separately presented monoid merely to state these
definitions. It does **not** prove cancellation/lcm/Garside normal forms or
normalizer splitting for that submonoid. Likewise an action groupoid or a
quotient built directly from the desired normalizer is not automatically
the subgroupoid generated by the article's actual ribbons.

## Pinned TauCeti and mathlib

Inspected the actual sources at TauCeti
`62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9` and mathlib
`65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9`, including the Coxeter Artin,
Matsumoto, longest-element, ordinary braid and generic normalizer-quotient
families. The relevant TauCeti tracked path inventory and focused source
searches found no Artin-monoid embedding, spherical Garside structure,
positive parabolic conjugation theorem, ribbon subgroupoid, ribbon
normalizer splitting, or complete ribbon presentation.

The available exact algebraic suppliers remain useful but weaker:

- `TauCeti.ArtinGroup M` is `PresentedGroup (artinRelationsSet M)`;
  `ArtinGroup.prod_map_gen_braidWord` proves its defining braid equality.
- `TauCeti.matsumoto cs f hbraid hω hω' hprod` identifies monoid evaluations
  of **reduced Coxeter words** with equal Coxeter product. It does not say
  arbitrary positive words equal in the Artin group are braid equivalent;
  that stronger implication would be the relevant monoid-embedding input.
- `CoxeterSystem.IsLongest w₀` in `LongestElement.lean` is defined by
  `∀ u, ℓ(u*w₀)+ℓ u=ℓ w₀`; its API proves involutivity, length reversal,
  uniqueness and parabolic-coset reversal. It concerns the Coxeter group,
  not an Artin monoid's divisibility lattice or a ribbon groupoid.
- TauCeti's `SpecificGroups/Braid/Basic.lean` defines ordinary braid groups
  as the type-`A` specialization of its actual Artin presentation. Its
  generator/braid/permutation and strand-inclusion results do not assert
  arbitrary spherical-Artin Garside or ribbon theorems.
- TauCeti's generic `Subgroup.normalizerQuotient` is exactly
  `N(H)/H`, and its lift API wraps the ordinary quotient universal property.
  It contains no spherical-Artin splitting result.

The native pinned mathlib already has the appropriate presentation
foundation:

```lean
PresentedMonoid (rels : FreeMonoid α → FreeMonoid α → Prop) :=
  (conGen rels).Quotient

PresentedMonoid.lift (f : α → N)
  (h : ∀ a b, rels a b → FreeMonoid.lift f a = FreeMonoid.lift f b) :
  PresentedMonoid rels →* N       -- [Monoid N]
```

See `Mathlib/Algebra/PresentedMonoid/Basic.lean:40,127`; `lift_of` computes
on generators, `ext` determines homomorphisms from generators, and
`mk_eq_mk_iff` identifies equality with the generated congruence.
These construct an actual Artin positive presentation and its canonical
map to the existing group, but they do not prove the map injective.

Pinned `Mathlib/GroupTheory/OreLocalization/OreSet.lean:50` defines an
`OreSet S` for `[Monoid R] (S : Submonoid R)` by weak right cancellation
and chosen `oreNum`, `oreDenom` satisfying
`oreDenom r s * r = oreNum r s * s`. The localization and its universal
property are in `OreLocalization/Basic.lean`; its
`universalMulHom` requires a monoid homomorphism taking denominators to
specified units. These are generic infrastructure after the actual Artin
Ore/cancellation inputs are proved. No such Artin instance was found.

For the final algebraic packaging, pinned mathlib's
`SemidirectProduct.mulEquivSubgroup` has inputs
`{H K : Subgroup G} [H.Normal] (h : H.IsComplement' K)` and concludes a
semidirect-product isomorphism with `G`. The complement condition is the
bijectivity of `(h,k) ↦ h*k`. It packages a proved splitting; it does not
prove that actual ribbons form the required complement.

# Landmark 3: actual Coxeter chambers and wall crossings

Source inspection on 2026-11-14. Parent snapshot: `b793bf9dd4c5c9637d8dde51c6a635f849b943c4`. This inventory contains proposed new statements and inspected supplier statements; it is not a build, axiom audit, or kernel-replay acceptance record. No mathematical source, vendor, cache, or configuration was changed in this pass.

## Decision and first authoring targets

Use the existing geometric representation and actual restricted arrangement. Native proofs from pinned mathlib and the already accepted Sign provider are the shortest compatible route. The searches below found useful proof patterns, but no ready theorem identifies these restricted Coxeter chambers with atomic ribbon galleries for every finite Coxeter group.

Author these statements in this order. The names below are **proposed**, not existing APIs.

1. **Uniqueness of a dominant orbit representative**, with arbitrary `I : Type*`, no finite-group assumption:

   ```lean
   theorem dominant_action_unique (M : CoxeterMatrix I) {φ : Dual I}
       (hφ : IsDominant φ) (w : M.Group)
       (hwφ : IsDominant (dualAction M w φ)) :
       dualAction M w φ = φ
   ```

   This is a direct extension of the proof of `Landmark1.dominant_fixed_iff`. Set `ψ = dualAction M w φ`; a left descent `i` of `w` makes `ρ(w⁻¹) αᵢ` negative. Dominance of `φ` gives `ψ αᵢ ≤ 0`, dominance of `ψ` gives equality, so the simple reflection fixes `ψ`. Apply induction to `sᵢ*w`. The existing `dominant_fixed_iff` then gives `w ∈ W_(zeroIndices φ)`. This avoids the crystallographic restriction of the inspected upstream uniqueness theorem.

2. **Sign cells are the actual connected chambers**. On `E := relativeSubspace J`, define

   ```lean
   realRegularSet M J := {φ : E | Landmark1.realRelativeRegular M J φ}
   sameRootSigns M J (φ ψ : E) :=
     ∀ r ∈ retainedRoots M J, (0 < φ.val r ↔ 0 < ψ.val r)
   ```

   For regular `φ`, prove

   ```lean
   connectedComponentIn (realRegularSet M J) φ =
     {ψ | ψ ∈ realRegularSet M J ∧ sameRootSigns M J φ ψ}
   ```

   The right side is an intersection of strict linear half-spaces, hence convex. A component has constant evaluation sign by `IsPreconnected.mapsTo_Ioi_or_Iio` (or `lt_of_ne`/`gt_of_ne`). Convexity gives the reverse component inclusion. This statement does not need finiteness; openness and finite enumeration do. Use the actual subtype topology and `continuous_evaluation`, rather than importing a second normed model. Then obtain open, convex, path-connected chambers in spherical type; closure is the associated weak sign cell, by a segment from a point of the nonempty strict cell.

3. **Standard facets and their transported versions**. Define

   ```lean
   standardFacet J : Set (Dual I) :=
     {φ | (∀ i ∈ J, φ (simpleRoot i) = 0) ∧
       ∀ i ∉ J, 0 < φ (simpleRoot i)}
   ```

   Prove its canonical point is `canonicalDominant J`, its image in `relativeSubspace J` is nonempty/open/convex, and every point there is `realRelativeRegular`. For the last assertion use the Sign root dichotomy: a positive root is coordinatewise nonnegative; a retained root has a nonzero coefficient outside `J`; a strict positive evaluation there makes the finite sum strictly positive. Negative roots follow by negation. The coefficient-support/annihilator equivalence is a genuine small bridge still to author.

   For `[Finite M.Group]`, `exists_dominant_dualAction` and point-stabilizer conjugation show every actual regular point is in a transported standard facet `dualAction M w '' standardFacet K` with `w * W_K * w⁻¹ = W_J`. Prove that such a facet is a full sign cell, hence a chamber; orbit uniqueness gives uniqueness modulo its pointwise parabolic stabilizer. Do not equate the conjugacy class of subsets with all subsets of the same cardinality.

4. **The elementary geometric wall**, with `a ∉ J`, `T = insert a J`, `K = parabolicTwistImage M T J`, and `x = Artin.projection M (elementaryMu M J a)`. In the fixed flat `Θ_J`, prove that `standardFacet J` and `dualAction M x '' standardFacet K` are distinct adjacent chambers, with common wall flat `Θ_T`. A useful first local lemma is:

   ```lean
   ∀ r ∈ retainedRoots M J,
     canonicalDominant T r = 0 →
       restrictedHyperplane J r = restrictedHyperplane J (simpleRoot a)
   ```

   Indeed the root-sign dichotomy and zero evaluation at `canonicalDominant T` force its support into `T`; on `Θ_J` its evaluation is its `a` coefficient times evaluation at `αₐ`. Retention makes that coefficient nonzero. Thus this point lies on exactly one *distinct* restricted hyperplane. Prove codimension one by the coordinate model, closure incidence for both facets, and their distinction. This supplies genuine adjacency without assuming it as a ribbon axiom. Distinction needs the actual nonparabolic/minimal representative fact for `x`; it is an explicit proof obligation, not a consequence merely of Artin degree positivity.

5. **Gallery distance and geodesicity**, after the preceding geometric facts. Define separating hyperplanes as actual distinct elements of `restrictedArrangement M J` on which two chamber signs differ. Prove adjacency changes exactly one such sign, gallery length is bounded below by their number, and a suitable generic segment gives a gallery crossing each separator once. Then establish the relative inversion/separation formula for transported facets, so the existing length-additive pair-lcm atomic words become actual geodesic galleries. `AtomicCoxeter` alone does not supply this conclusion. In particular, do not identify one atomic edge with Coxeter length one: its weight is `ℓ(π μ)`, which can be larger than one.

All five stages retain arbitrary index universes. Obtain `Finite I` from `Geometry.finite_index M`, then use `Fintype.ofFinite` locally where finite intersections/sums are needed. Avoid `I : Type` restrictions and unnecessary reindexing of geometry. For `J = univ`, `Θ_J = 0`, there are no retained hyperplanes and exactly one chamber; there are no outside atomic labels. For `J = ∅` these definitions recover the ordinary dual chamber arrangement. The rank-zero case is included.

## Existing actual models and accepted local inputs

Inspected the complete relevant parent files, not just their descriptions:

* `ArtinNormalisers/Theorem18/Geometry.lean`: `Vector I := I →₀ ℝ`; `Dual I := Module.Dual ℝ (Vector I)`; topology induced by `dualCoordinatesHomeomorph : Dual I ≃ₜ (I → ℝ)`. `relativeSubspace J` is the submodule annihilating the selected simple roots. `root M w i := M.toCoxeterSystem.geometricRepresentation w (simpleRoot i)`. `roots M` consists of these actual orbit roots; `retainedRoots M J` additionally requires a nonzero restriction to the flat. `restrictedHyperplane J r` is the kernel of that restriction and `restrictedArrangement M J` its image over retained roots, so repeated/proportional roots give one actual hyperplane. `Complement M J` is the subtype of pairs of real flat points on no `H × H`. `finite_index`, `roots_finite`, `retainedRoots_finite`, and openness of the actual complement are already proved under `[Finite M.Group]`.
* `ArtinNormalisers/Theorem18/NormalizerAction.lean`: `dualAction M : Representation ℝ M.Group (Dual I)` satisfies `dualAction M w φ v = φ (ρ(w⁻¹) v)`. `mem_relativeSubspace_iff_fixed` identifies the flat with the pointwise fixed space of the actual generated parabolic. * `landmarks/ArtinLandmarks/Dominant.lean`: `IsDominant φ := ∀ i, 0 ≤ φ (simpleRoot i)`; `zeroIndices φ := {i | φ (simpleRoot i) = 0}`. Literal key conclusion:

  ```lean
  dominant_fixed_iff (hφ : IsDominant φ) (w : M.Group) :
    dualAction M w φ = φ ↔
      w ∈ Artin.coxeterParabolic M (zeroIndices φ)
  ```

  Also `canonicalDominant_fixed_iff` and `pointwise_flat_fixed_iff` for every `J`, with no finite-group assumption.
* `landmarks/ArtinLandmarks/RegularStabilizer.lean`: under `[Finite M.Group]`,

  ```lean
  exists_dominant_dualAction (φ : Dual I) :
    ∃ u, IsDominant (dualAction M u φ)
  realRelativeRegular M J (φ : relativeSubspace J) : Prop :=
    ∀ r ∈ retainedRoots M J, φ.val r ≠ 0
  realRelativeRegular_fixed_iff φ hφ g :
    dualAction M g φ.val = φ.val ↔ g ∈ Artin.coxeterParabolic M J
  ```

* `landmarks/ArtinLandmarks/Covering.lean` proves actual complement-pair stabilizers, free quotient action, actual orbit covering, and its fundamental-group short exact sequence. It defines no real chamber, facet, crossing, or gallery.
* `ribbons/ArtinRibbons/AtomicCoxeter.lean`: `projection_positiveToParent`, `projection_parentSimpleLift`, `degree_eq_coxeterLength_of_simple`, `elementaryMu_degree_eq_coxeterLength`, and

  ```lean
  AtomicWord.coxeter_length_additive_of_simple (p : AtomicWord M X Y)
      (h : ∃ w, p.eval = positiveToParent M (positiveSimpleLift M w)) :
    M.toCoxeterSystem.length (Artin.projection M p.eval) = p.coxeterWeight
  AtomicWord.pairLcm_coxeter_length_additive p a b
      (he : p.eval = pairRibbonLcm M X.indices a b) :
    M.toCoxeterSystem.length (Artin.projection M p.eval) = p.coxeterWeight
  ```

  Here `coxeterWeight` is the sum of the Coxeter lengths of the traversed elementary projections. `AtomicWord.length` counts atomic edges and is a different quantity. `RibbonLcm.pairRibbonLcm_weakPrefix_join` already proves the algebraic weak-prefix join for the two longest-element ratios; no upstream weak-order geometry needs to be invented as a hypothesis.

**Action convention.** An actual ribbon `r : J → K` conjugates `W_J` to `W_K` by `x⁻¹ W_J x`, for `x = π(r)`. Consequently the target chamber drawn in the *source* flat is `x · C_K ⊆ Θ_J`. Appending `s : K → L` gives `x y · C_L`, agreeing with `AtomicWord.eval` putting the first traversed label on the left. Neither this convention nor geometric equivariance should be silently inverted.

## TauCeti: actual open-cover groupoid gluing

All paths in this section are relative to `TauCeti/`, and names are in
`TauCeti.FundamentalGroupoid` unless explicitly qualified.

### Literal spaces, diagram, and colimit

[`Topology/Category/TopCat/Cech/Diagram.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/Topology/Category/TopCat/Cech/Diagram.lean)
defines, for `X : TopCat` and `U : ι → Opens X`,

```lean
abbrev CechIndex (ι : Type u) := OrderDual {s : Finset ι // s.Nonempty}
def cechIntersection (s : CechIndex ι) : Opens X := s.1.inf U
```

Here nonempty means the **index finite set**, not an assumption that the
intersection itself contains a point. Empty and disconnected intersections
are allowed. The topological diagram consists of the actual subtype spaces
`TopCat.of (cechIntersection U s)` and actual inclusions, ordered by reverse
inclusion of finite index sets.

[`AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/Cech/Diagram.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/Cech/Diagram.lean)
defines

```lean
def cechDiagram : CechIndex ι ⥤ Grpd :=
  cechTopDiagram U ⋙ _root_.FundamentalGroupoid.fundamentalGroupoidFunctor
```

`cechCocone U` is the image under that same Mathlib functor of the cocone
of inclusions into `X`. Its point is definitionally the actual fundamental
groupoid of `X`, not a freely generated substitute.

The main endpoint in
[`Cech/Colimit.lean`, line 125](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/Cech/Colimit.lean#L125)
is exactly

```lean
def isColimitCechCocone (hU : IsOpenCover U) : IsColimit (cechCocone U)
```

There is no connectedness, contractibility, good-cover, finiteness, or
arrangement hypothesis. The only additional hypothesis is that `U` covers.
The result is a strict categorical colimit in `Grpd`; it is not a theorem
that the geometric realization of a nerve is homotopy equivalent to `X`.
That distinction prevents upgrading it to an asphericity theorem.

No inspected repository outside the separately assigned TauCeti/OpenAI search
supplies the full equivariant restricted-arrangement comparison. The closest
actionable generic supplier is **qinz1yang/differential-geometry's genuine
two-open fundamental-groupoid Seifert–van Kampen theorem**, with an eight-file
project import closure. Its literal theorem uses actual topological spaces
and proves a pushout; it does not assume the pushout as a structure field.
It is an alternate generic supplier, not an accepted imported proof.

The other especially relevant search result, the Chen-ranks development,

polygonal-path homotopies. It supplies neither the chamber presentation nor
the required comparison/equivariance in the inspected source. Its basic
convex-ball cover is not itself a nerve comparison.

The parent's `Complement M J` is the subtype of

from the actual dual coordinates. Retained roots discard those identically

The desired supplier must connect this actual complement to a groupoid
whose generators are geometric positive crossings and whose relations have

generators, not formal inverses. A homotopy-equivalence transport theorem
alone does not construct that equivalence. A generic open-cover theorem
alone does not identify its colimit with the ribbon/Deligne presentation.

## Literal strongest generic theorem

At the pinned qinz1yang commit,
[`DifferentialGeometry/Topology/VanKampen/FullGroupoid.lean`](https://github.com/qinz1yang/differential-geometry/blob/13c41a632efb8fbf93101c8a20f2a9214ab33240/DifferentialGeometry/Topology/VanKampen/FullGroupoid.lean)
defines `fullGroupoidSquareIsPushoutStatement U V` as the actual `IsPushout`
in `Grpd` of these four objects and continuous inclusion-induced functors:

```text
FundamentalGroupoid (U ∩ V) → FundamentalGroupoid U
             ↓                         ↓
FundamentalGroupoid V       → FundamentalGroupoid X.
```

The exact exported declaration is:

```lean
theorem seifertVanKampen {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (U V : Set X)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hV : IsOpen V) (hcover : U ∪ V = univ) :
    fullGroupoidSquareIsPushoutStatement U V
```

The namespace is `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen`. No path-connectedness,
simply-connectedness, local-contractibility or dimension assumption is hidden
in this declaration. In `Evaluation.lean`, `LocalFunctorData U V G` contains
only functors from the two actual fundamental groupoids into `G`, plus their
agreement after restriction to `U ∩ V`. Its `extension` is **constructed** by
path subdivision and evaluation, descended through proved homotopy invariance;
its extension and uniqueness properties produce the pushout proof. No
extension-existence or desired pushout field is assumed in that data.

Its project closure is exactly these eight modules, in a possible dependency
build order:

1. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.Subdivision`
2. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.CoveredPath`
3. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.Evaluation`
4. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.HomotopyGrid`
5. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.CellIdentity`
6. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.GroupoidTelescope`
7. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.HomotopyInvariance`
8. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.FullGroupoid`

All remaining imports are mathlib modules: fundamental groupoid basics,
composable arrows, groupoids, categorical pushouts, product homotopies,
metric-space lemmas and subpaths. A lexical scan with comments removed found
no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide` or `unsafe` token in this closure.
That scan neither checks elaboration nor certifies transitive axioms.

Possible actual application: choose genuine open subsets of `Complement M J`,
prove they cover, and apply the theorem to construct/characterize its
fundamental groupoid from the restrictions. For a finite chamber-indexed
cover, one would still have to derive the iterated/multiple-overlap colimit,
identify all intersection components and their paths/relations, and prove the
Deligne/ribbon presentation and normalizer equivariance. These are substantial
new bridges, not consequences of this theorem's name. The separately examined
TauCeti Čech theorem may be a more direct generic API; do not import two
parallel van Kampen implementations without need.

If selected after the actual-cover route is fixed, verification should copy
only this unchanged eight-module closure into an isolated test package using
the project's existing Lean/mathlib pins, preserving Apache headers and
binding upstream/local hashes. A proposed initial command, **not run here**,
is `lake build DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.FullGroupoid` after
declaring that test library. Then inspect its elaborated statement and audit
all declarations of all eight modules, allowing only `propext`,
`Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`; run the existing project's supported
single-module checker form for each module. The upstream package's older
toolchain is not a reason to replace this project's pins. A successful
upstream build alone would not certify the port or its application.

## Literal definitions behind the other close results

The Chen-ranks repository's `ChenRanks.AffineArrangement d ι` has a finite
index type and fields `normal : ι → (Fin d → ℂ) →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ`, `offset : ι → ℂ`,
nonzero normals, and pairwise distinct equation zero sets. It defines

```lean
def Complement := {x : Fin d → ℂ // ∀ i, A.normal i x ≠ A.offset i}
```

with the induced topology. Its `actualPolygonalApproximationHomotopy`, for an
actual `γ : Path x y` in `A.Complement`, constructs a fixed-endpoint path
homotopy from the actual polygonal approximation to the full subpath of `γ`.
`ActualComplementBall` contains an actual center/radius, positivity and proof
the ambient ball lies in the complement; `actualComplementBallAt` constructs
such a ball at each point from proved openness, and
`mem_actualComplementBallBaseSet_at` proves the resulting cover property.

This is not a surrogate space. To apply it here requires a proved finite
complex-coordinate identification of the relative real-pair vector space,
complexification of the distinct retained hyperplanes, and equality of the
two removed sets/topologies. Such a bridge is mathematically possible but was
not constructed by this search. These results still do not supply homotopy
**completeness** of chamber relations or equivariance. Existing project
path-connectedness already addresses a simpler part of this geometry.

The jacobian repository's `TwoOpenVanKampen` expands to: every path-connected
topological `Z : Type` covered by open simply-connected `U,V` with
path-connected intersection is simply connected. Its
`Jacobians.RiemannSphere.VanKampen.twoOpenVanKampen_holds` proves that exact
proposition by actual subdivisions, spokes and path-homotopy telescoping.
It is a genuine corollary, but cannot replace a presentation of the generally
nontrivial fundamental groupoid of a hyperplane complement.

The pytop file is a concrete rejected assumed-conclusion case:
`VanKampen.Pushout datum A` contains only `i₁`, `i₂`, and their compatibility
for **additive commutative** groups. `pushout_universal` is given an arbitrary
`u : A →+ K` plus
`hu₁ : ∀ g₁, u (po.i₁ g₁) = f₁ g₁` and
`hu₂ : ∀ g₂, u (po.i₂ g₂) = f₂ g₂`; its conclusion is just the conjunction
of those equations for each pair `(g₁,g₂)`. Its proof is
`fun g₁ g₂ => ⟨hu₁ g₁, hu₂ g₂⟩`. It constructs no universal factor or
topological path identification. The file's own Scope paragraph states this
limitation; no false topological theorem is attributed to it.

Polylean's `FundamentalGroupoid` is an instance on a
`CombinatorialTwoComplex`: its homs are quotients of combinatorial edge paths
by an inductively defined relator homotopy. It uses a custom `Groupoid` and
`SerreGraph` reversal. It does not prove those are topological paths of a
realized space, so naming it a fundamental groupoid does not fill the bridge.

The two Kang repositories' exact useful form is
`SSet.realizationSimplicialHomotopy (H : SSet.Homotopy f g) :
(SSet.toTop.map f).hom.Homotopy (SSet.toTop.map g).hom`, and the analogous
homotopy of classifying maps from a natural transformation `α : F ⟶ G`.
These relate actual realizations, but no map from our complement, chamber
good cover, or equivariant homotopy inverse is present in the inspected file.

## Existing mathlib APIs and duplication screen

At the project's existing pin,
`FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.equivOfHomotopyEquiv (e : X ≃ₕ Y)` already gives
an equivalence of the actual fundamental groupoids. The neighboring
`homotopicMapsNatIso` constructs the natural transformation of path-class
functors from an actual continuous homotopy. The sphere-six-complex wrapper
then takes endomorphism groups via fully faithfulness; this supplies no new
geometric comparison.

`Convex.contractibleSpace (hs : Convex ℝ s) (hne : s.Nonempty)` already proves
`ContractibleSpace s` in a real topological vector space with continuous
addition and scalar multiplication. This is suitable for genuine convex
finite intersections of a proposed good cover once their inclusion/cover
conditions have been proved. The existing dual-coordinate topology supplies
the appropriate continuous vector-space structure. None of these facts
identifies a nerve with the actual complement by itself.

Searched the pinned fundamental-groupoid/simplicial-groupoid modules and
related file names for a ready-made open-cover comparison. No such result
was located in that bounded inspection; this is not an assertion about all
future or uninspected mathlib declarations.

## Search record, provenance and limits

Used `gh search repos`, `gh search code`, raw pinned GitHub URLs via Python's
HTTPS client, and isolated `/tmp` shallow clones. Search terms included
`Salvetti`, `DeligneGroupoid`, `HyperplaneArrangement`, `FundamentalGroupoid`,
`vanKampen`, `hyperplane complement`, `complexified`, `GoodCover`, and
`nerve contractible`, with Lean/`.lean` filters and a second pass explicitly
excluding `openai/math` and `leanprover-community/mathlib4`.

The observed `Salvetti`, `DeligneGroupoid`, and explicit excluded-repository
`Deligne groupoid`, `complexified`, `GoodCover`, `nerve contractible` queries
returned no results. This is a GitHub-index/API observation, not proof of
worldwide absence. Several earlier requests received HTTP 429/403 search-rate
errors; the affected later query families were retried successfully in the
second pass. Search is bounded by indexing, branch selection and result caps.

The temporary machine inventory is `/tmp/m3-other-inventory.json`. It has
the twelve source-inspected repositories, full commits, licenses, source
hashes, declaration names, application/disposition, reading limits and
explicit false build/audit/replay/acceptance flags. It separately lists
twenty-eight repositories appearing as code-search hits, without calling
those hits proof use. Query records are in
`/tmp/milestone3-other-search.json` and `/tmp/m3-search-round2.json`;
the full qinz import/hash inventory is
`/tmp/m3-qinz-fullgroupoid-closure.json`. These temporary inventories are
provided for the root's central provenance register; this report is the only
repository file authored by this task.

No mathematical defect was established in the consulted source passages.
Rejected applicability, missing local formalization, unknown reuse permission
and unexecuted verification are recorded as such, not as article defects or
false mathematics. No external proof is accepted from theorem marketing,
badges, source appearance or `#check`.

# Theorem 1.8: additional arrangement-source candidates

Research date: 2026-11-14. Scope: exact pinned-source inspection of the two
additional repositories identified by root. Only this new report was edited.
No Lean sources, frozen reviews, configuration or provenance were changed.
No dependency was imported, built, installed, axiom-audited or kernel-replayed;
no shared cache was touched. No external supplier is accepted by this report.

## Decision

Neither candidate supplies Deligne asphericity for finite real simplicial
arrangements, a comparison of the **ordinary complex topological complement**
with a Salvetti or Deligne model, or the relative normalizer fundamental-group
identification needed in Theorem 1.8.

OrlikSolomon does have substantive, actual finite affine arrangements,
localization rings and open **scheme** complements, with explicit comparison
isomorphisms. These are not mocked topological interfaces, but their category
and topology differ from the article's `X_J^C`. Atlas's named hit is an
affine-arrangement predicate, with no complement construction or theorem.
No immediate vendoring is recommended for this theorem.

## adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon

- Repository: <https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon>.
- Inspected SHA: `1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c`.
- Complete Git tree response: 586 entries, not truncated.
- Toolchain: `leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0-rc2`.
- Manifest mathlib: `6db5db0d2279846cc8fb25901bd53221d37a77d8`.
- Manifest Verso: `71a2035b44e7f54a797ce799fd1b03cdd3a44684`.
  The Lake configuration separates the library from the Verso book.
- License: Apache-2.0, confirmed in root LICENSE and source headers.
- Read-only source snapshot:
  `/tmp/theorem18-additional/orlik-full/OrlikSolomon-1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c`.

Fetched the exact Git tree and an archive of the immutable commit. Searched
all 419 files under `OrlikSolomon/` for the relevant topology terms; inspected
the declarations and proof passages below. This is not a complete
line-by-line mathematical review of the repository.

### Real finite affine arrangements and algebraic complements

[`Geometry/Arrangement.lean`, lines 68–72](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Geometry/Arrangement.lean#L68)
defines

```lean
structure Arrangement (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] where
  hyperplanes : Finset (AffineSubspace k V)
  isHyperplane_of_mem' : ∀ H ∈ hyperplanes, IsHyperplane H
```

This is actual finite affine-subspace data over an arbitrary field; it can
be specialized to `ℂ`. Its restriction/deletion API uses affine pullbacks
and discards empty or full-space traces as appropriate. The definitions do
not include a real structure, chamber simpliciality, or the Euclidean
topology on the complement.

[`Geometry/Complement.lean`](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Geometry/Complement.lean)
defines `Arrangement.ComplementRing := Localization 𝒜.equationSubmonoid`.
The submonoid is generated by equations of the arrangement's hyperplanes.
This is an actual ring construction; it is explicitly **not** the type of
points in a topological complement. `ComplementRing.isLocalizationAway`
relates it to localization at a product of equations.

[`Geometry/Schemes/Complement/Basic.lean`](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Geometry/Schemes/Complement/Basic.lean)
adds actual open subschemes, in namespace `OrlikSolomon.Geometric`:

- `hyperplaneComplement H` (line 101) is the complement of the image of
  the closed immersion of the hyperplane scheme into affine space.
- `complementOpens 𝒜` (line 136) is the intersection of these open sets.
- `complement 𝒜 : Over (Spec (.of k))` (line 164) is the corresponding
  open subscheme, with its restricted structure sheaf.
- `complementIsoSpec 𝒜` (line 251) constructs an isomorphism to
  `spec (CommAlgCat.of k 𝒜.ComplementRing)`, using equality of ranges of
  actual open immersions. `complementIsoSpec_hom_comp` proves it lies over
  the ambient affine space.
- `complementMap` (line 431) constructs a scheme morphism from an affine
  map `φ : W →ᵃ[k] V` under
  `∀ K ∈ 𝒜, ℬ.Covers (K.comap φ)`. Here `Covers` means empty or a member
  of `ℬ`. `complementMap_comp_complementι` verifies the ambient square.
- `complementIso` (line 564) constructs a scheme isomorphism from an
  affine equivalence that identifies the hyperplane sets by pullback.

These are positive algebraic-geometry results. Their carriers are scheme
points with the Zariski topology, not vectors in `ℂ^n` with its usual
topology. Setting `k := ℂ` does not change this distinction. No proved
complex-points/analytification comparison to the article's topological
complement was found.

### Exact meaning of the proposed projective-complement hit

Read
[`Interface/ProjectiveComplement.lean`](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Interface/ProjectiveComplement.lean)
and the relevant definitions in `Interface/ProjectiveSpace.lean`.
`projectiveSpace k n` is `Proj` of the polynomial ring over `k`, as a
scheme over `Spec k`. In namespace `OrlikSolomon.Interface`:

- `complementOpens 𝒜` (lines 37–44) is the complement of the union of the
  projective **scheme** hyperplanes.
- `complement 𝒜` (line 49) is this open subscheme over `Spec k`.
- `complementSchemeIso` (line 113) and `complementIso` (line 129) compare
  that actual open subscheme with the library's other projective-complement
  construction. They are categorical scheme isomorphisms, not a Salvetti
  comparison or a passage to a fundamental groupoid.
- `complement_isAffine_smooth` (line 145) assumes `𝒜.Nonempty` and proves
  affineness and smoothness of the scheme complement.
- `complementIso_hom_appTop_projectiveRatio` and `isUnit_ratio` compare
  global sections and prove invertibility of ratios of hyperplane equations.

The statements quantify over arbitrary fields and projective dimensions.
They contain no simplicial-arrangement hypothesis and no homotopy,
asphericity, covering-space or normalizer conclusion. In particular,
`complementIso` does not fill any of the topological comparison gaps in
the Theorem 1.8 source inventory.

### Cohomology examples and absence of a formal singular bridge

Read the relevant sections of
[`Examples/ProjectiveOrdinary.lean`](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Examples/ProjectiveOrdinary.lean).
`singleHyperplaneCohomologyEquiv`, `nonempty_basis_points_grading_one`, and
related declarations take a supplied `T : OrdinaryTheory ...`. The explicit
three-point finite-field examples include the zero coefficient theory.
These test the specified cohomology interface and its edge cases; they are
not proofs about classical `π₁` or `K(π,1)` spaces. The final interface
examples test actual affine/smooth scheme complements and equation ratios.

[`Cohomology/Axioms.lean`, immediately before `OrdinaryTheory`](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Cohomology/Axioms.lean#L118)
explicitly states:

> “This is a mathematical argument, not a formal one: no singular instance
> exists in Lean, so a statement about singular cohomology still needs a
> value of this structure for it.”

The same passage distinguishes the constructed nonzero characteristic-zero
algebraic de Rham instance from the zero theories. I do not characterize
the whole cohomology development as vacuous: the relevant limit is that
neither algebraic de Rham cohomology nor a conditional ordinary-theory
isomorphism supplies the required topological asphericity or relative
fundamental-group equivalence.

### Verification and reading limits

The calculated `OrlikSolomon.*` source import closure of
`Interface.ProjectiveComplement` contains 22 modules, 11,052 source lines,
all present, with remaining imports in mathlib. A source screen found no
`sorry`, `admit`, custom `axiom` declaration, `unsafe def/theorem`, or
`opaque` declaration in that closure. This is not a transitive axiom audit.
The temporary list is
`/tmp/theorem18-additional/orlik-projective-interface-closure.txt`.

Read the audit tool's introductory design and the replay script. They
describe private-level import inspection, checking all project declarations
against the three usual axioms, and per-module kernel replay. Their source
and README claims do not establish that any such checks were run here.
No build, fresh audit or replay was performed by this task.

Full-source term searches under `OrlikSolomon/` found no occurrence of
`Deligne`, `Salvetti`, `asphericity`, `aspherical`, `SimplyConnectedSpace`,
`FundamentalGroup`, `HomotopyGroup`, `ComplexManifold`, `Analytification`,
or `SingularCohomology`. This is bounded textual evidence, not a proof that
every equivalent formulation is absent. The explicitly documented missing
singular instance and the inspected exact statement types are stronger
evidence for rejecting the proposed topological use.

## facebookresearch/atlas-lean

- Repository: <https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean>.
- Inspected SHA: `8e813e63090880e090494edfb55c7602cd961987`.
- Complete Git tree response: 24,571 entries, not truncated.
- Toolchain: Lean `v4.35.0`.
- Manifest mathlib: `56a005855ea17e0b0958f73ec801ae140b0a1679`.
- Root LICENSE contains Apache-2.0 text, preceded by the repository's
  statement that the codebase is not intended for ML-model development.
  No code was copied or proposed for reuse.

Read the full
[`MathlibExt/Combinatorics/Poset/Basic.lean`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/8e813e63090880e090494edfb55c7602cd961987/MathlibExt/Combinatorics/Poset/Basic.lean).
Its only arrangement declaration is in namespace `MetaMathlibExt`, line 230:

```lean
def IsHyperplaneArrangement {K V : Type*} [Field K]
    [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V]
    (E : AffineSubspace K V) (A : Set (AffineSubspace K V)) : Prop :=
  A.Finite ∧ ∀ H ∈ A, H ≤ E ∧ (H : Set V).Nonempty ∧
    Module.finrank K H.direction + 1 =
      Module.finrank K E.direction
```

This is a faithful finite codimension-one affine-arrangement predicate.
The module's other definitions are Möbius multiplication and flag
vectors. It provides no complement, continuous map, groupoid, or theorem
about arrangements, and therefore no direct missing proof supplier.

Also read
[`MathlibExt/AlgebraicGeometry/LineArrangement.lean`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/8e813e63090880e090494edfb55c7602cd961987/MathlibExt/AlgebraicGeometry/LineArrangement.lean).
It defines finite projective-plane line sets, multiplicities, pairwise
intersection points and their Harbourne constant; its substantive results
identify singular points and show their existence. These concern incidence
and counting, not complement topology.

Searched the complete pinned tree's path inventory for arrangement,
complement, Salvetti, Deligne and asphericity candidates. I did not download
or text-search every Atlas source file, audit its transitive definitions,
or inspect its unrelated `WantedExt` and historical `v1` mathematics.
No broad code-search queries were used, and none of the negative result
depends on a rate-limited search response.

## Remaining obligations and disposition

Neither source changes the missing bridges recorded in `search-openai.md`:
the actual relative complex complement; the finite simplicial arrangement
and normalizer action; a verified comparison to its own topological
Salvetti/Deligne model; asphericity; the ribbon/normalizer vertex-group
identification; and compatibility of all covering and algebraic exact
sequence maps, including basepoints and path-composition conventions.

The OrlikSolomon affine restriction API could be reconsidered if the
project later needs algebraic arrangement incidence or coordinate-ring
theorems. That possibility alone does not justify adding its dependency
closure to this topological proof. Atlas's predicate is only a definition,
not a proof of an outstanding prerequisite.

No mathematical error in either inspected source or the original article
was established. A category/topology mismatch and an explicitly unformalized
comparison are reuse limitations, not allegations of false statements.

No directly applicable formal supplier for the **relative hyperplane
complement** in Theorem 1.8 was found in the inspected sources. Both
repositories contain a substantial ordinary Artin Salvetti development,

isomorphism for its combinatorial quotient. They do not provide the needed
comparison with the article's relative complexified arrangement complement,
the action of `N(W,J)` on that complement, or the compatible normalizer
fundamental-group exact sequence.

The combinatorial Salvetti definitions are substantive: the base space is
constructed by gluing actual spherical Coxeter permutahedra. I found no
definition replacing the target space by a point, and no conclusion is
merely assumed as a field in the inspected endpoint definitions. This does

## Target checked against the article

X_J^C = (Cone(J)° × Cone(J)°) \ ⋃_{H∈H_J} (H × H).

arrangement with open simplicial chambers. Corollary 6.14 invokes Deligne's

Theorem 6.7 identifies the normal-cover exact sequence with the algebraic
normalizer sequence through the Deligne groupoid, its `N(W,J)` quotient,
and the reduced ribbon groupoid. Remark 3.25, PDF page 12, explicitly
states that the `N(W,J)` action need not be chamber-transitive.

Consequently, an ordinary Coxeter–Salvetti theorem cannot be applied just

## Proof closure, source-hole and comparator limits

Following actual `OAI.*` imports from `SalvettiProjection.lean` gives
617 modules, approximately 59,545 source lines, all present in the downloaded
ArtinGroups subtree. The temporary closure inventory is
`/tmp/lemma28-full-search/theorem18-openai-salvetti-closure.txt`.
The import parser includes apostrophes in Lean module identifiers; the
tracked `MulBlockDiagonal'Entry.lean` import is present.

The contractibility route passes through:

- spherical positive-region contraction and a countable directed cover;
- contractibility of the Deligne coset realization;
- lower-fiber contractibility for the lifted-cell-to-Deligne map;
- an abstract weighted-poset realization criterion;
- reindexing and the nerve/weights homeomorphism.

The inspected statements retain their hypotheses rather than introducing
a field asserting the final Salvetti theorem. The source screen over all
617 modules found no word `sorry`, `axiom`, `admit`, `unsafe`, or

`ComparatorChallenges/HarmonicArtin.lean` deliberately contains `sorry`.

are not evidence that an axiom audit or independent kernel replay was run
in this task. I did neither.

The accompanying preprint's `build/sections/topology.tex` was read. It
discusses ordinary Coxeter permutahedra and cites classical Salvetti and
spherical-asphericity inputs. Its prose is not an additional Lean proof
of a general real-arrangement-complement comparison.

| Required input | What these sources actually supply | Missing work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Actual `X_J^C` from root hyperplane restrictions | Ordinary `M`-indexed lifted cells and permutahedral gluing | Define the geometric dual/root representation, relative intersection and hyperplane family; prove the correct complex complement and topology. |
| Finite central simplicial relative arrangement | Finite Coxeter spherical cells | Prove the relative arrangement's finite/simplicial hypotheses. A restricted arrangement is not automatically a Coxeter arrangement. |
| Salvetti comparison for a finite real simplicial arrangement | Internal nerve/weights/model-cell homeomorphisms | Prove a comparison between the actual relative complement and its arrangement Salvetti/Deligne model, using actual continuous maps and homotopies. |
| Relative asphericity | Contractibility theorem for ordinary Artin lifted cells | Formal Deligne asphericity for general finite simplicial arrangements, or another proof for these specific restrictions. |
| `N(W,J)` free properly discontinuous action | Free ordinary-Artin deck action on ordinary lifted cells | Construct and verify the geometric normalizer quotient action and its covering. |
| `π₁(X_J^C/N(W,J)) ≃* N(A,J)` | `π₁(SourceSalvetti M) ≃* Artin M` | Relative Deligne/ribbon groupoid comparison and the reduced ribbon vertex-group isomorphism, or an equally faithful alternative proof. |
| Isomorphism of the two exact sequences | Existing algebraic Lemma 2.8; an unrelated ordinary Salvetti `π₁` isomorphism | Prove compatibility with covering monodromy and algebraic projection, including basepoints and path-composition/opposite conventions. Abstract group isomorphisms alone are insufficient. |

The empty-relative-subset special case might eventually benefit from the
ordinary Salvetti source after verification and comparison. It does not
establish the arbitrary-`J` theorem, and narrowing the target is not proposed.
No supplier is recommended for immediate vendoring solely on the present
evidence.

## Other nearby hits and search limits

`ParabolicIntersections/RelativeInitialStabilizer.lean` mentions van der
